title: add multi-timescale stability aggregator and rate-aware safeguard
author: Maya Chen
description: Context and motivation: We see frequent short-lived latency blips that spike minute-level percentiles but decay within 10-30 minutes, and separately sustained regressions that emerge across hours. Existing canary logic treats short and long signals the same, resulting in unnecessary rollbacks or noisy alerts. This PR adds a Multi-Timescale Stability Aggregator that fuses minute-, hour-, and day-level fingerprints to distinguish transient noise from sustained regressions and introduces a Rate-Aware Safeguard that gates canary traffic when throughput drops coincide with latency increases. Design summary: the aggregator consumes existing metric streams (p50/p95/p99, qps, error-rate) and produces a composite stability score per canary cohort that weights signals by their persistence and recency. The weight schedule is adaptive: minute-level signals get high sensitivity but are discounted quickly; hour-level signals influence short-term decisions; day-level signals govern sustained rollouts and regression alerts. The rate-aware safeguard watches normalized QPS deltas and uses an exponential backoff policy to throttle canary weight when latency worsens and throughput drops simultaneously; it allows automated partial cutback instead of full rollback. What changed (high-level): implemented a lightweight aggregator in canary/aggregator, added detector that consumes fused fingerprints in detectors/, introduced a small runtime gate in runtime/ that can be configured per-deployment, added a protobuf for the guard config, documentation and integration tests, and chart defaults for staged rollout. Commits summary: "initial aggregator skeleton and data model"; "implement timescale fusion logic and scoring"; "add rate-aware safeguard and backoff controller"; "integration tests and docs"; "chart defaults and small fixes". Files touched: see file list above. Testing and validation: unit tests for fusion weights and scoring, integration test that replays historical traffic with injected blips and sustained regressions and asserts correct gating decisions, load smoke test to ensure no extra latency introduced by aggregation. Performance: aggregator runs in O(n) per cohort per window and uses a small memory footprint; local microbenchmarks show <1% CPU at typical canary scales. Rollout plan: staged rollout to perf-canary namespace at 5% of canary traffic, monitor stability_score and canary_gate events for 48h, increase to 25% and then full if no sustained alerts. Backout: config flag to disable aggregator and safeguard; immediate rollback plan coordinated with SRE. Checklist: implement core fusion algorithm; add guard config & proto; add tests; update docs; update helm values; smoke performance test. Review notes and conversation (summary): Liam: "Nice separation of signals — can we make the hour-window weight configurable per-customer? Also please add a short lived metric for aggregate time to compute the score." Author (Maya): "Exposed hour/day weights in GuardConfig proto and added a compute_latency_ms metric emitted by the aggregator." Priya: "The exponential backoff parameters need bounds to avoid starving canaries under noisy QPS; add sane defaults and a guardrail." Author: "Added min/max bounds and unit tests that assert backoff stays within limits under synthetic noise." Anders: "Suggest adding a debug endpoint to sample fused fingerprints for triage." Author: "Added /debug/canary/fingerprint (disabled by default behind feature flag) and documented usage." Merge details and CI: CI pipeline passed on second run after flake fix; checks: unit-tests (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), e2e-smoke (pass). Merge method: squash and merge. Release notes: "Add Multi-Timescale Stability Aggregator to reduce noise-induced rollbacks and Rate-Aware Safeguard to throttle canary weight when throughput drops with latency increases; configurable via GuardConfig and helm values." Impact and follow-ups: monitor stability_score false-positive rate for 2 weeks; add telemetry to correlate stability score vs user-facing errors; consider ML-based weight tuning in follow-up.
